title: From a River in Gilead to the Inference Distributions of Large Language Models: Covert Dialect Bias and Linguistic Profiling at Scale

bias_targets.methodology: Adapting the matched-guise paradigm to compute length-normalized log-probabilities of positive and negative housing-relevant adjectives for meaning-matched sentences across four English dialects (Standard American English, African American Vernacular English, Nigerian Standard English, and Nigerian Pidgin).

Analyzing covert stereotype associations (e.g., threat, unreliability) activated by racialized Black English varieties (AAVE and Nigerian Pidgin) to measure covert racial prejudice embedded in model probability distributions.

Evaluating xenophobic exclusion by measuring the probability elevation of adjectives like 'foreign' when models evaluate Global South postcolonial dialects (Nigerian Standard English and Nigerian Pidgin) in community integration contexts.
